reason: The cited lines show an HTTP client performing GET requests to a supplied URL, following redirects, reading response.text, and returning that content as TextContent. This is not arbitrary host code execution. It is a SINK because it sends a request to a supplied/agent-chosen URL/host. It returns remote response bodies, which can be attacker-controlled, so UNTRUSTED is supported. Because the fetched URL is not shown to be restricted and the returned content is placed into the agent context, these lines also support returning non-public reachable URL content such as localhost/intranet HTTP resources.
